CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's topics and subtopics, covering the definition and origins of heuristic evaluation, all ten of Nielsen's usability heuristics, and the evaluation process; used by learners and instructors to navigate or plan the module's content.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: This page outlines the module's core topics, introducing heuristic evaluation as a structured usability inspection method, explaining its purpose, origins, and advantages over other evaluation approaches, and serving as a navigational overview for learners beginning the module.

Artifacts.Name: Heuristic_Evaluation_and
Artifacts.Description: A printable HTML document providing comprehensive reading material on heuristic evaluation, including its definition, Nielsen's ten heuristics, and the evaluation process; used by learners as a self-contained reference for studying the full module content.

Artifacts.Name: List Explain Nielsen's
Artifacts.Description: This activity presents a scenario involving a banking app login screen with three specific usability problems and asks learners to identify which of Nielsen's 10 heuristics are violated, helping them practice applying the principles to real-world interface issues.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to Heuristic Evaluation
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces heuristic evaluation as a structured usability inspection technique, explaining what it is, why it is widely used, and how evaluators assess a user interface against recognized usability principles — serving as a conceptual foundation before learners engage with the method hands-on.

Artifacts.Name: Nielsen's Ten Usability Heuristics
Artifacts.Description: This reading presents all ten of Nielsen and Molich's usability heuristics, explaining each principle and its application to interaction design so that learners can use them as a reference framework when conducting their own heuristic evaluations.

Artifacts.Name: The Heuristic Evaluation Process
Artifacts.Description: This reading walks through the step-by-step process for conducting a rigorous heuristic evaluation, distinguishing a valid structured inspection from an informal review and guiding both learners and instructors on correct methodology.

Artifacts.Name: Severity Rating
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to assign severity ratings to identified usability problems, covering the criteria that separate critical barriers from minor cosmetic issues so that learners can prioritize findings and help development teams allocate resources effectively.

Artifacts.Name: Aggregating Findings Across Evaluators
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers how to consolidate usability findings from multiple independent evaluators into a single unified list, explaining why no single evaluator catches every problem and how to merge, deduplicate, and reconcile separate reports.

Artifacts.Name: Writing Formal Heuristic Evaluation Reports
Artifacts.Description: This reading describes how to structure and write a formal heuristic evaluation report — including the components, language, and level of detail needed to communicate findings credibly to stakeholders such as project managers who were not present during the evaluation.

Artifacts.Name: Evaluating Peer Prototypes
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces a peer-evaluation assignment in which learners independently apply the full heuristic evaluation process to three prototypes created by classmates, moving beyond controlled practice examples to real, unvetted interface designs.
